newsitem.title: ITALY: UN agency reports cattle plague epidemic in Africa.
newsitem.headline: UN agency reports cattle plague epidemic in Africa.

text.p: The U.N.'s Food and Agriculture Organisation said on Monday that Kenya and Tanzania had been hit by a major cattle plague epidemic and called for urgent aid to avert a disaster that could have big food security consequences.

FAO said in a statement that rinderpest, a highly contagious and lethal disease affecting cattle and wild animals such as buffaloes, eland and giraffes, had spread swiftly in eastern and southern Kenya and into Tanzania.
It said the outbreak, considered the worst in the last 15 years, comes at a time when parts of eastern Africa are suffering from serious drought and tightening food supplies.
FAO expert Mark Rweyemamu said in the statement that drought aggravated the problem because pastoralists moved cattle in search of water and animals came into contact with the disease.
"(It) will, unless checked, sweep through Tanzania and on into southern Africa," he said.

"Substantial donor support is urgently needed for a transboundary regional control programme to prevent a major livestock and wildlife catastrophe that could have serious consequences for food security in eastern and southern Africa," the FAO statement said.

Kenyan and Tanzanian vetinary and wildlife specialists are monitoring the situation in collaboration with FAO and the Organisation of African Unity. FAO said it had already started an emergency assistance project for Tanzania.
Rinderpest is caused by a virus and causes fever and intestinal ulcers.
